transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-05
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood CSM), Dr. Nina Park (Cascade CTO), Marco (Head of MLOps), Aisha (Procurement)
---
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Quick roll call — Jordan Meyers from Redwood, with Priya our solutions engineer and Liam our CSM. How are you all?
[00:07] Nina: Hi Jordan, hey Priya, good thanks. Marco and I are here and Aisha from procurement, thanks.
[00:12] Marco: Yep — morning.
[00:15] Jordan: Cool. The main agenda I sent was renewal terms and the multi-region add-on you requested — EU and APAC — and then any security/audit questions Aisha has. Is that accurate on your side?
[00:24] Nina: Yes, that's right. We're up for renewal next month and we want to move from month-to-month to a committed contract, plus add two regions to reduce latency for our clinicians in London and Singapore.
[00:34] Aisha: And procurement will need the SOW and pricing in order to proceed.
[00:38] Priya: Quick clarification — are you targeting full traffic in the new regions day one, or a phased ramp/canary?
[00:44] Marco: Phased. We'll start with read-only inference for non-prod workloads, then increase. But we need baseline numbers for p95 latency under current workloads.
[00:52] Jordan: Perfect. We'll propose a committed tier that matches your current average qps with headroom for peaks and a canary plan. Priya, do you want to walk through the proposed technical approach?
[00:59] Priya: Sure. So, for multi-region we can replicate model variants into eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1. For a dedicated reserved pool we recommend a small dedicated GPU pool per region to keep cold-starts low and 95th perc latency predictable. We'll leverage automatic prefix KV cache so repeated prompts for the EHR templates hit cache and reduce token cost.
[01:20] Marco: When you say KV cache, do you mean you keep patient prefixes? We need to be careful about PHI.
[01:24] Priya: Right, good point. The cache is configurable and we can set TTLs and encryption at rest with your KMS. We do not persist customer data beyond the retention window you set in the config.
[01:32] Nina: On the KMS note, we need HSM-backed keys and a clear audit trail for key usage. SOC 2 scope is a must.
[01:39] Liam: We can provide our SOC 2 report and also a redacted audit artifact showing KMS integration patterns with HSM. We'll include network diagrams for VPC peering and the private control plane we recommend for Private deployments — though for now you're on hosted/dedicated.
[01:51] Aisha: Procurement will want to see the SLA, the overage policy, and termination terms. Also any pass-through fees for egress between regions.
[01:58] Jordan: Understood. Pricing note: adding regions is priced as an add-on with a reserved capacity multiplier — effectively a discount versus spinning up ad-hoc capacity. We'll show the delta in the worksheet. For overage we propose a soft cap with automatic burst and then overage billed at a pre-agreed rate — we can make that explicit in the SOW.
[02:14] Marco: Can you hold the current rate if we sign a 12-month commitment? We saw a price increase on token rates earlier this year elsewhere and want stability.
[02:22] Jordan: Yes, the 12-month reserved contract will lock the unit pricing for the duration. We can provide a few tiers: base committed qps, a moderate headroom tier, and a high-availability tier that reserves extra pool for bursting.
[02:35] Nina: What's the lead time to get eu-west and ap-southeast pools up and running? We have compliance reviews next week so speed matters.
[02:43] Priya: Typical provisioning is 48–72 hours for hosted capacity, but since this is reserved/dedicated pools we can pre-provision within 5 business days once the order is in and we have network details for VPC (if you go private). For hosted dedicated we just need the capacity commitment.
[03:01] Marco: If we pre-provision, can we run a 7-day perf test to validate p95 and throughput before we flip traffic?
[03:06] Priya: Absolutely. We'll stand up test endpoints and run your traffic profile. We'll need a representative sample from you — QPS, average seq length (tokens), and peak windows.
[03:14] Marco: I'll share that by Friday.
[03:17] Aisha: Procurement question — do you accept PO and is there an e-invoicing flow? Also do you require any vendor-specific contract edits?
[03:24] Jordan: We accept PO and have a standard MSA that procurement usually signs. We can accept most reasonable commercial redlines; anything security-related we loop in legal and security to scope. We typically avoid changes to our liability caps but we've negotiated on enterprise deals before.
[03:36] Nina: Any limitations on data residency? If the model processes PHI, can we ensure the inference stays in-region or within our VPC?
[03:44] Priya: For hosted dedicated pools we control the region. For Private deployment we can run in your VPC or on-prem to guarantee residency. With hosted/dedicated we provide network isolation and encryption; but if you need full in-VPC compute, that's handled by Private.
[03:58] Marco: Cost delta between hosted dedicated and private for our scale? Ballpark.
[04:02] Jordan: Private has a platform fee plus support and often an upfront engagement. On a 12-month horizon, dedicated reserved is typically 20–30% lower TCO than pure hosted burst depending on utilization, but private can be lower for sustained very high throughput because you amortize infra. We'll model both in the worksheet.
[04:19] Aisha: Can you also include timeline to on-prem in the deck? Our legal may insist on an option.
[04:24] Jordan: Yes, we'll add a short on-prem path and estimate.
[04:27] [04:27] -- 10 minute mark summary by Jordan -- We proposed tiers, discussed KV cache and PHI controls, agreed on a 7-day perf run and required artifacts: SOC 2, network diagram, KMS/HSM notes. Action items listed.
[04:40] Priya: Back to technical specifics — for latency we target p95 under 250ms for simple prompts in-region. For longer sequences or higher temperature stochastic generation latencies increase; we'll share guidance on batching and quantization profiles for cost/latency trade-offs.
[04:55] Marco: The 250ms p95 is fine for clinician-facing quick lookups; for complete note generation we expect higher but still want predictability.
[05:03] Priya: We'll set up a continuous monitoring dashboard for token breakdowns and p95 traces per route; that ties into Redwood Console so you can set alerts if latency or per-token cost regresses.
[05:12] Marco: Good, can Liam give access to the console for our infra team?
[05:16] Liam: Yes, I'll provision a role-based access and send invites; RBAC will let you restrict sensitive routes.
[05:23] Aisha: One more procurement item — do you do revenue recognition-friendly invoicing? We have to schedule payments across quarters.
[05:29] Jordan: We can accommodate net-30 with staged invoicing on committed tiers. We'll coordinate with finance on payment schedule.
[05:34] Nina: Regarding benchmarks, can Redwood run a side-by-side comparison with Anthropic models? We want to justify the switch for our board.
[05:42] Priya: We avoid direct benchmarking of competitors in the quote but we can run perf and quality evals on your prompt set against the model family you use and provide scorecards. If you want a competitor run we can discuss what datasets and IP constraints exist, but we typically focus on objective metrics.
[05:58] Marco: That works — we'll provide representative prompt set and a pass/fail rubric.
[06:03] Jordan: Great. Any other blockers on the procurement or security side?
[06:06] Aisha: Just the usual — SOC 2, data processing addendum, and proof of KMS/HSM. Also need indemnity language and liability limits clarified.
[06:16] Jordan: Understood. We'll share standard clauses and flag non-negotiable items.
[06:20] [06:20] Priya: Technical note — when we provision dedicated pools in new regions we recommend a small canary routing rule that sends 5–10% traffic initially and auto ramps after monitoring. Also we can pin specific model versions per route to prevent surprise regressions.
[06:36] Marco: How do rollbacks work if a model variant shows quality regression after a deploy?
[06:40] Priya: We support immediate traffic split and automatic fallback to a previous pinned model. Redwood Optimize also can detect quality regressions based on your eval prompts and alert you.
[06:49] Nina: That alerting is critical for us. Include retention windows for logs and traces in the docs you send.
[06:54] Liam: Will do. We'll include 90/365 retention options with pricing.
[06:59] Jordan: Ok, let's summarize next steps — I'll send the pricing worksheet and term summary with the 3 tier options, Priya will spin up test endpoints for a 7-day perf run in EU and APAC, Liam will send SOC 2 & KMS artifacts and console invites, Marco will share traffic profile and prompt set, Aisha will confirm procurement timeline.
[07:17] Aisha: Sounds good. If procurement gets the SOW by Monday we can route quickly.
[07:20] Jordan: We'll target sending the docs by EOD Sunday.
[07:23] [07:23] Minor crosstalk and wrap-up.
[07:26] Jordan: Thanks all — we'll follow up with calendar invites for the perf run kickoff and the updated quote.
[07:30] Marco: Thanks everyone.
[07:33] Nina: Thanks.
[07:35] End of call.

Notes about transcript quality: Some speaker attribution is approximate, occasional word substitutions ("KV cash" vs "KV cache"). References to artifacts: pricing worksheet (link to be shared), SOC2 report (redacted), network diagram (diagram.pdf).
